# DayRecall

> DayRecall is an AI memory app for Apple Watch and iPhone, made for people who forget things. During the hours you choose, it listens, keeps what was said as text on your iPhone (no audio is kept), and answers questions about your day with the exact words and where they came from. Everything stays on your devices: there is no account and no DayRecall server.

DayRecall 是一款适用于 Apple Watch 和 iPhone 的 AI 记忆 App，写给容易忘事的人：在你选定的时段里替你听着，把说过的话变成文字存在 iPhone 上（不留音频），随时回答关于这一天的问题，并给出原话和出处。

## Key facts

- Devices: best with Apple Watch; an iPhone can also listen on its own. When both listen, the day is one timeline, and what both heard is shown once. Requires an iPhone with iOS 26 or later and Apple's on-device speech recognition (iPhone 12 or later recommended; iPhone 11 models and iPhone SE (2nd generation) lack it). Apple Watch is optional: watchOS 26 or later (Series 6 and later, SE (2nd generation) and later, any Ultra).
- The watch does not need the iPhone nearby. It holds what it heard and hands it to the iPhone every two hours, or as soon as the two reconnect.
- On the watch, an in-house ultra-light speech model (2,561 parameters, custom accelerated inference kernels) checks every 0.1 seconds whether someone is talking and keeps only speech.
- Lab results for that model: 99.9% of speech kept on the AMI Meeting Corpus test set; 95% of background-noise time skipped on the DEMAND dataset.
- Internal testing: on Apple Watch Series 11, listening adds about 0.9% battery per hour; on iPhone 17 Pro Max, 3 minutes of conversation are processed in 17 seconds.
- Speech becomes text on the iPhone, and the audio is cleared once it has been transcribed; only the text is kept. Answers come from Apple's on-device model. Nothing leaves the iPhone unless the user turns on their own cloud API or hands a day to an AI app.
- Optional speaker marking: after reading five short cards (about a minute), the user's lines are marked "Me" and everyone else "Other 1", "Other 2" and so on. Only the user's voiceprint is stored, on the iPhone.
- Optional Health clues: after the user turns on Settings › Health, DayRecall reads sleep, steps and walking distance, workouts, heart rate and resting heart rate from the Health app, to label parts of the day (walking, working out, heart rate faster than usual) and to find what was said during an activity the user asks about (for example, "before bed"). Read only; nothing is stored, and it is not sent to DayRecall or anyone else, except that the user can choose, when handing a day to an AI app (off by default, and asked each time), to add short labels such as "Walking" (no numbers) to the file. No medical conclusions and no health advice.
- Optional multilingual transcription: up to three languages in one conversation, each part transcribed in the language it was spoken in, with translation into the user's language. The app itself is available in 14 languages.
- Languages depend on Apple's on-device technology and the iOS version: transcription on Apple's speech recognition (English, Chinese (Mandarin, China mainland), Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), Cantonese (China mainland), Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Swedish, Danish, Turkish, where the iPhone supports them); translation on Apple's translation (supported pairs depend on the iPhone and iOS version; transcription support does not guarantee translation support); answers and to-dos on Apple Intelligence (iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, iPhone Air, iPhone 16 or later; device and Siri language set to a supported language; not currently available on iPhones bought in mainland China, where answers can use the user's own cloud API).
- Status: in beta, coming soon to the App Store.
